prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

WASHINGTON (CNN)  -- While nearly all maritime activity on the Potomac River will be halted on Inauguration Day, a handful of Mall-goers will sail from Virginia to Washington on water taxis. Some people will cross the Potomac River via water taxi on Inauguration Day. Working closely with the United States Coast Guard, the Potomac Riverboat Company, based in Alexandria, Virginia, plans to ferry up to 3,200 passengers from across the frigid Potomac on seven climate-controlled boats. The service is partially a response to the closure of all bridges from Virginia to D.C. on Inauguration Day, a measure that prompted an uproar among Virginia residents. According to maritime authorities in charge of the region, PRC is the only company being allowed to taxi across the river on the 20th. "Because the taxi service provided us with a security plan that we examined and deemed adequate to provide good security, I granted them a waiver to operate at an increased security level," National Capitol Region Port Captain Brian Kelley says. "The taxis are going to operate on a strict schedule and a strict route." The Coast Guard established a temporary security zone on waterways in the National Capitol Region, stepping up restrictions day-by-day leading up to 11 p.m. on January 19. At that point, all vessels must be docked and only boats with an approved sail plan will be allowed to operate. John Lake, a ship captain and the general manager of the company, said the sail plan he submitted was approved only a week ago and details nearly every move taxis will make. "All the departures are scheduled times. And those departures are supposed to leave on-time," Lake said. "We have to call in on each departure to the Coast Guard, let them know we're preparing to get under way, and get the permission, basically, to get under way." The boats depart the Alexandria Marina for the 40-minute trip beginning around 6 a.m. and must be docked on the southwest D.C. shore by 10 a.m. From there, it's a cold, mile-long walk to the Mall, so Lake has some advice for passengers. "Show up early to get through the security check and dress warm," he said. "It's going to be nice and toasty on the boat, but not so much outside." Return trips, tentatively scheduled for around 6 p.m., are not allowed to depart D.C. until after the inaugural parade events have concluded and President Obama is secured. In keeping with the Coast Guard's security measures, Lake says all passengers must arrive at least an hour early for a full screening. Passengers that want to stay in D.C. after the early evening departures will have to find other transport back across the Potomac. PRC Vice President Charlotte Hall says tickets went on sale Monday and the initial response from customers has been enthusiastic.

John Lake, a ship captain and the company’s general manager, said the sail plan he submitted was approved only a week ago and details nearly every move the taxis will make.

“All the departures are scheduled times. And those departures are supposed to leave on-time,” Lake said. “We have to call in on each departure to the Coast Guard, let them know we’re preparing to get under way, and get the permission, basically, to get under way.”

WASHINGTON (CNN) — Most boat traffic on the Potomac River will be suspended for Inauguration Day, but a limited number of people heading to the National Mall will be able to travel from Virginia to Washington by water taxi.

The Alexandria, Virginia-based Potomac Riverboat Company (PRC) is coordinating with the U.S. Coast Guard to transport as many as 3,200 passengers across the icy river aboard seven heated and climate-controlled vessels.

The option was created in part because every bridge leading from Virginia into Washington, D.C., will be closed that day—a decision that caused widespread anger among Virginians. Regional maritime officials say PRC is the sole operator authorized to provide cross-river taxi service on January 20.

National Capitol Region Port Captain Brian Kelley said he approved an exemption after reviewing the company’s security proposal and determining that it met the requirements for operating under heightened security. He added that the water taxis will be required to follow a tightly controlled timetable and route.

The Coast Guard has imposed a temporary security zone across National Capitol Region waterways, with restrictions increasing each day until 11 p.m. on January 19. After that deadline, every vessel must be at its dock unless it has an authorized sailing plan.

PRC general manager and boat captain John Lake said the plan he submitted—approved only a week earlier—specifies nearly every movement the taxis will make. Each departure has a fixed time and must occur punctually, he said. Before every trip, the company must contact the Coast Guard, report that a vessel is preparing to leave, and receive clearance to proceed.

Boats will begin departing Alexandria Marina at about 6 a.m. The journey will take approximately 40 minutes, and all vessels must reach their docks on Washington’s southwest waterfront by 10 a.m.

Passengers will then face a roughly one-mile walk in the cold to reach the Mall. Lake advised travelers to arrive ahead of time for security screening and to wear warm clothing. Although the boats will be comfortably heated, he noted, conditions outside will not be as pleasant.

Return service is provisionally planned for around 6 p.m. However, boats cannot leave Washington until the inaugural parade activities are over and President Obama has been secured.

Under Coast Guard security rules, every passenger must report at least one hour before departure to undergo a complete screening. Anyone choosing to remain in Washington after the early-evening return trips will need to arrange another way back across the Potomac.

PRC Vice President Charlotte Hall said ticket sales opened Monday and customers responded with strong enthusiasm.

counterfactuals.output:
## Reaching the National Mall from Virginia by Water Taxi on January 20

For Virginians traveling to Washington for an inauguration or another major January 20 event, a water taxi can avoid the region’s most congested roads and Metro stations. The usual Virginia departure point is the **Alexandria City Marina**, with some special-event services also originating at **National Harbor**. Boats generally arrive at **The Wharf in Southwest Washington**, about a mile from the National Mall.

A water taxi does not, however, deliver passengers directly into the Mall’s secured area. Travelers must walk from the dock and pass through the appropriate pedestrian security checkpoint.

### Confirm the special-event schedule

January is outside the normal peak boating season, so riders should not rely on an ordinary summer timetable. On January 20, operators may provide a limited, reservation-only schedule with designated outbound and return sailings.

Passengers should:

- Consult the operator’s **January 20 special-event schedule**, not its regular timetable.
- Buy tickets in advance; popular departures can sell out.
- Arrive at the Virginia dock **at least 30 to 60 minutes before departure**.
- Allow additional time for weather, Coast Guard restrictions and passenger screening.
- Confirm whether the ticket is tied to a particular boat or return time.

Because inauguration arrangements change from one presidential term to another, exact sailing times must be checked with the operator—typically **City Cruises/City Experiences’ Potomac Water Taxi**—for the relevant year. Service can be delayed or canceled because of ice, high winds, security zones or Coast Guard orders.

### Where the boat leaves passengers

The Washington landing is normally at **The Wharf**, along Maine Avenue SW. From there, passengers can walk north toward the National Mall. Depending on fencing and crowd-control measures, the most direct-looking route may be blocked, so riders should follow signs and instructions from police, National Guard personnel and event staff.

The walk to the Mall is roughly 20 to 30 minutes under ordinary conditions, but on January 20 it can take much longer. Only designated entrances allow access to ticketed or public viewing areas.

### Expect two layers of security

Water-taxi passengers may encounter screening before boarding and again when entering the National Mall.

At the marina, the operator or law-enforcement officers may:

- Check tickets and identification.
- Inspect bags.
- Prohibit weapons and hazardous materials.
- Restrict large luggage, coolers, bicycles and oversized items.
- Require passengers to board only their assigned sailing.

At the Mall, the federal security rules are usually stricter. Prohibited items commonly include firearms, knives, explosives, large bags, glass containers, alcohol, drones, laser pointers, large signs with rigid supports and other objects considered dangerous. Umbrellas, folding chairs, backpacks and insulated containers may also be restricted in particular zones.

Passengers should carry as little as possible and review the official prohibited-items list before leaving home. Passing a marina inspection does **not** guarantee that an item will be allowed through a Mall checkpoint.

### Bridge closures make the boat attractive—but complicate backup plans

Major January 20 security plans often close or restrict Potomac River crossings, especially those closest to the ceremony. The **Arlington Memorial Bridge** commonly faces extensive closures because it leads directly toward the Lincoln Memorial. Other bridges—including the **Theodore Roosevelt, 14th Street, Key and George Mason bridges**—may have lane closures, vehicle restrictions or security checkpoints.

Pedestrian and bicycle access can also be limited. Closure times and affected bridges vary by year and can change at short notice.

Travelers should not assume that a friend, taxi or ride-share driver will be able to collect them near the Mall. Roadblocks may force vehicles several blocks away, and congestion can continue well into the evening. Anyone driving to the Alexandria marina should also verify parking rules and reserve extra time.

### Return trips are often the biggest limitation

A water-taxi ticket should not be treated like an unrestricted shuttle pass. Special-event service may require passengers to return:

- From the same Washington dock.
- On the sailing printed on the ticket.
- Within a limited afternoon or evening departure window.
- Only as part of a round-trip reservation.

Missed return boats may not be rebooked, and later sailings may be full. Some operators do not sell one-way return tickets on the day of the event. Boats also cannot necessarily wait for passengers delayed by crowds or security checkpoints.

Before leaving The Wharf for the Mall, riders should note the last boarding time and plan enough time to walk back through closed streets. A prudent approach is to begin returning to the dock **at least 60 to 90 minutes before boarding**, or earlier if officials report heavy pedestrian congestion.

Travelers should also have a backup plan, such as walking to an operating Metro station, using Virginia Railway Express if special service is offered, or arranging pickup outside the restricted zone. The backup should not depend on crossing a bridge that authorities have closed.

### Final checklist

Before traveling, confirm:

1. The water taxi is operating on January 20.
2. The exact Virginia departure dock and check-in time.
3. The assigned outbound and return sailings.
4. Weather and Coast Guard service alerts.
5. The official Mall security and prohibited-items rules.
6. Current bridge, road and pedestrian closures.
7. A backup route if the return boat is missed or canceled.

The water taxi can be one of the least stressful ways to approach downtown Washington from Virginia, but only for passengers who reserve early, travel light and treat the return schedule as firm.

### Seven Climate-Controlled Boats to Carry Inauguration Attendees Across the Potomac

Seven climate-controlled boats will transport inauguration attendees across the Potomac under an approved sail plan designed to keep the special-event service orderly, secure and on schedule.

The crossing is expected to take approximately 40 minutes. Passengers should treat that estimate as travel time only: boarding, security procedures and movement to and from the docks may add substantially to the overall trip. Organizers are therefore advising attendees to arrive well before their assigned departure time. Late arrivals may not be accommodated once boarding closes or a vessel leaves the dock.

The approved sail plan establishes the route and operating framework for the seven-boat service. Travelers should follow all instructions from transportation staff, vessel crews and security personnel, and should use only the boat and departure window listed in their official travel information. Because access around the inauguration may be restricted, passengers should not assume they can switch sailings or reach the dock quickly by another route.

Although the vessels are climate-controlled, parts of the journey will still involve exposure to winter weather. Attendees may have to wait outside, walk along waterfront approaches, stand on docks or pass through open boarding areas. Wind along the Potomac can make temperatures feel considerably colder, particularly in the early morning.

Passengers should dress warmly and in layers, with a winter coat, hat and gloves. Comfortable, weather-appropriate shoes are also recommended, as docks and nearby walkways may be cold, wet or slippery. Any inauguration dress clothing should be supplemented with practical outerwear for the trip.

Before leaving, attendees should confirm their assigned departure location and time, allow extra time for security and boarding, and bring any required ticket, credential or identification. They should also check official transportation notices for weather-related or operational updates.

The central message is simple: arrive early, follow the approved sail plan and prepare for the cold—even though the 40-minute ride itself will be aboard a climate-controlled boat.
